#Notes on the simulation of JWST data for the EIGER program (PID 1243).
#Machine used: hyperion.ethz.ch


#First time: 
conda create -n eiger python
conda activate eiger
pip install mirage
pip install jwst


#Later times:
#I recommend running these things within a screen on the hyperion machine. In this case your scripts will continue running when you disconnect
screen 
conda activate eiger


#Directories:
cd /scratch/EIGER/

#In here you find:
#apt_files -- Files generated by the APT program. These contain the information on the various exposures and instrumental setup of our program (ID #1243). For some reason mirage likes to save its logs here
#catalog_data -- This contains the simulated JADES catalogs and the template QSO spectrum. There is a simple python script that allows you to plot a single JADES spectrum
#reduce_pipeline -- working directory to use the pipeline, currently empty
#simulate_mirage -- working directory to simulate images, contains python scripts to run and a folder (MIRAGE_DATA) with download calibration files (688 GB!)


###SIMULATING DATA WITH mirage
cd simulate_mirage

#In order to simulate the imaging data, please use the following command. Note that this just simulates a few images, it's straightforward to modify. There are quite a few input parameters to modify.

python simulate_images.py

#Simulating grism data. This is in principle split in two scripts as part of this procedure can be parallelsed more efficienty. 
#Step 1: Creating the catalog of sources and Spectral catalog. If you want, this script can also simulate the grism images but it will be slower. There are many input parameters to vary.
#Note that you need to run simulate_images.py once before as that creates the yaml files (once the yaml files are there this is not necessary)

python simulate_grism_catalog.py

#Step 2: Multiprocessing. After you created the catalogs, it is possible to brute-force multiprocess as follows:

./multiprocess_grism.sh

#This spans a lot of processes that run the script "simulate_grism_core.py". You defeinitely want to do this within a screen as it is printing a lot of terminal output.




#The output/simulated images are stored in the output folder. The images that the pipeline needs are "jw01243001001_01101_00012_nrcb5_uncal.fits"
#A few words on their structure:
#jw 01243  001  001_01101_00012_nrcb5_uncal.fits  01243 is our program ID. 001 is the target 001 is the visit 00012 is the exposure numbernrca/nrcb means module a/b 12345 correspond to the camera (with 1234 being SW and 5 LW).
#the *linear.fits images are linearised and are useful for visual checks. There are numerous other output files that could be useful, e.g. the seed images.




#Final step of Mirage is ordering of the files. THis will be useful for reducing the data
python organise_files.py





conda deactivate
